title: CTC maximum per child, TY2027
question: IRS first official inflation-adjusted maximum Child Tax Credit per qualifying child under IRC section 24(a), as modified by section 24(h)(2), for tax year 2027, in nominal dollars, first print.
resolutionSource: First IRS annual inflation-adjustment revenue procedure or equivalent IRS release for tax year 2027
resolutionRule: Resolve to the first official IRS published value for the maximum Child Tax Credit under IRC section 24(a), as modified by section 24(h)(2), for taxable years beginning in 2027. Use the nominal dollar amount per qualifying child in the first IRS annual inflation-adjustment revenue procedure or equivalent IRS release for tax year 2027. If later IRS forms or instructions revise the amount, ignore them unless the first IRS release is formally corrected. The BLS September 11, 2026 CPI release fixes an input to the formula but is not the resolving publication. The statutory formula uses section 1(f)(3) chained-CPI cost-of-living adjustment with 2024 substituted for 2016 and rounds any increase down to the next lowest multiple of $100.

drivers: Public Law 119-21 raised the maximum Child Tax Credit from $2,000 to $2,200 for taxable years after 2024
IRC section 24(i)(2) indexes the $2,200 maximum after 2025 using chained CPI with 2024 as the base year
Rounding down to the next lowest $100 creates a discrete threshold near 4.545 percent cumulative inflation from the 2024 base
BLS May 2026 CPI data showed elevated inflation momentum, making a $2,300 print more likely than $2,200
The main downside risk is disinflation or data revision leaving the September 2025-August 2026 average below the statutory threshold

reasoning.text: Forecast for TY2027 maximum Child Tax Credit per child

The resolver is the first official IRS dollar value for the maximum Child Tax Credit per qualifying child for tax year 2027. This is the maximum under IRC section 24(a) as modified by section 24(h)(2), not the refundable portion under section 24(h)(5), a phase-in rate, a phaseout threshold, or a monthly equivalent.

reasoning.result: Fetched existing related catalog cell ctc-monthly-max-ty2027 with historical monthly values 2021 = 300, 2022 = 167, 2024 = 167, 2025 = 167, and 2026e = 167; records also showed ctc-maximum-per-child-ty2027 as the obvious canonical maximum-per-child slug.

reasoning.call: Opened GovInfo Public Law 119-21, section 70104, Extension and enhancement of increased child tax credit.
reasoning.result: Fetched statutory values: section 70104 changes IRC section 24(h)(2) from $2,000 to $2,200, applies after December 31, 2024, and section 24(i)(2) indexes the $2,200 amount after 2025 using section 1(f)(3) with 2024 substituted for 2016; section 24(i)(3) rounds any increase down to the next lowest multiple of $100.

reasoning.call: Opened IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 for tax year 2026 annual inflation adjustments and the IRS tax-year 2026 inflation-adjustment release page.
reasoning.result: Fetched IRS first-print context: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 says Public Law 119-21 provides a maximum Child Tax Credit of $2,200 for taxable years beginning in 2025, adjusted for inflation after December 31, 2025; for taxable years beginning in 2026, section 4.05 lists maximum credit amount = $2,200 and refundable portion = $1,700.

reasoning.call: Opened BLS May 2026 CPI release for inflation momentum relevant to the remaining statutory chained-CPI months.
reasoning.result: Fetched inflation context: CPI-U rose 0.5 percent in May 2026 and 4.2 percent over 12 months; April 2026 12-month CPI-U was 3.8 percent; energy rose 23.5 percent over 12 months; C-CPI-U rose 4.0 percent over 12 months and 0.6 percent in May on a not seasonally adjusted basis.

reasoning.call: Opened BLS September 2026 release calendar to verify when the final August CPI input becomes public.
reasoning.result: Fetched release schedule: Consumer Price Index for August 2026 is scheduled for September 11, 2026 at 08:30 AM Eastern; this fixes the last month in the September 2025-August 2026 CPI window used for calendar-year 2027 tax inflation adjustments, but the resolving source remains the later IRS first-print tax-year 2027 inflation-adjustment publication.

reasoning.text: Base-rate/reference class: recent official IRS annual inflation adjustments for this exact parameter show the base moving from the old $2,000 regime to $2,200 under Public Law 119-21, with TY2026 still $2,200 because the first year of chained-CPI growth over the 2024 base did not produce a full $100 rounded-down increase. The outside-view prior is therefore sticky at $2,200 or a one-notch move to $2,300, not a continuous estimate.

Simple discrete nowcast prior: using the May 2026 chained-CPI momentum and the remaining June-August window, I assign roughly 25 percent to a $2,200 IRS print, 60 percent to $2,300, 12 percent to $2,400, and 3 percent to policy or inflation outcomes outside that range. I do not use a richer time-series model because the rounded statutory threshold dominates the forecast and only three monthly CPI inputs remain before the formula is fixed.

Mechanism decomposition: level is the statutory $2,200 base; momentum comes from elevated 2026 inflation, especially the May 2026 C-CPI-U 4.0 percent 12-month increase; the one-off component is energy-price pressure that may fade before August; policy risk is small because Public Law 119-21 already made the credit permanent, but Congress could still amend section 24 before the IRS print.

Counter-consideration: the no-change $2,200 case remains plausible if June-August chained CPI is soft enough, if preliminary C-CPI-U revisions lower the 12-month average, or if IRS applies a technical convention that leaves the cumulative adjustment just below the $100 threshold. An upside outside the interval would require a legislative expansion or unusually high inflation producing a $2,500-or-higher official value; a downside outside the interval would require repeal or a statutory cut.

Threshold math: under section 24(i)(2)-(3), the TY2027 increase is floor_to_$100(2200 * COLA_2027_with_2024_base). The first $100 increment requires COLA >= 100 / 2200 = 4.545 percent. TY2026 remained $2,200, implying the one-year 2025-over-2024 COLA generated less than $100 after rounding. By May 2026, BLS reported C-CPI-U +4.0 percent over 12 months and CPI-U +4.2 percent, so the two-year 2026-over-2024 window is likely above 4.545 percent by August 2026. The 80 percent interval of $2,200 to $2,400 corresponds to the central 97 percent of the discrete prior after excluding only the low-probability legislative-cut and $2,500-plus inflation-tail cases; the point is the modal rounded amount, $2,300.

Review disposition: accepted the blocking critique that the BLS September 11, 2026 CPI date fixes an input but is not the IRS resolving publication; changed the resolver to the expected IRS TY2027 first-print release with a stable IRS placeholder URL, clarified the refundable-portion exclusion, added a discrete nowcast prior, and tied the interval to probability mass over rounded statutory outcomes.
